title: Be the linker

milestone.title: Visual Studio and the Build Pipeline

description:
Write `linkErrors(objects)`, a tiny linker that only checks symbols.

Each `ObjectFile` has a name, the symbols it **defines** and the symbols it **needs**. The function returns the list of errors, in this order:

1. For every symbol defined in more than one object file: `"duplicate X"`, once per symbol, with symbols in alphabetical order.
2. For every symbol needed by some object file but defined in none: `"unresolved X"`, once per symbol, with symbols in alphabetical order.

A symbol that an object file both needs and defines itself is fine. No errors means an empty list.

```
main.obj   defines main         needs addBonus, printf
score.obj  defines addBonus     needs (nothing)
crt.lib    defines printf
-> no errors

without score.obj -> { "unresolved addBonus" }
```
hints: First gather everything: count how many times each symbol is defined, and collect the set of all needed symbols.
`std::map` and `std::set` keep their keys sorted, so looping over them gives alphabetical order for free.
A symbol is a duplicate if its count is more than 1, and unresolved if it is needed but has no entry in the counts.
lessonTitle: Preprocessor, Compiler, Linker: Who Does What
